gap_reasons: The new contribution evaluates conditional obstructions and an explicit design-gap interval for a phenomenon already reported in [Stoye (2012)](https://stoye.economics.cornell.edu/docs/CeMMAP-Stoye.pdf), rather than solving the general fixed-design minimax problem. The strict design comparison establishes no quantitative excess-regret bound, so its shrinking contamination interval does not establish the practical magnitude of the allocation penalty. The TL;DR correctly distinguishes necessity from global sufficiency and contains no stale matched-frontier claim. These restrictions make the package a specialized extension and constrain its projected paper score; routine rewriting cannot supply the missing general decision certificate or quantify the design penalty. Construct an all-size floor-attaining Bernstein table at K_n, with proved coefficient bounds and nonnegative global endpoint slacks, thereby converting the conditional obstruction into an exact fixed-arm threshold.
proof_attempt_summary: One D0 solve round derived exact conditional capacities, an explicit strict design-gap interval, the complete n=2 correspondence and support transition, the n=3 frontier, and a general conditional-to-global bracket. The stratumwise construction fails global endpoint slack at n=40, while the contrast-only cubic forces an illegal coefficient 43/40 at n=4; neither failure rules out a bivariate remainder. The n>=4 exact global frontier and excess-regret magnitude remain open, two dependency declarations are unrepaired, and the discovery-stage TeX proofs have not been formalized in Lean.
tldr: Target ambiguity can make fixed balanced allocation strictly worse than independent fair assignment even with the same total sample size. Separate hypergeometric score capacities yield an explicit necessary floor threshold \(K_n\), and a weighted harmonic mean places the known independent threshold \(I_n\) strictly below it for every \(n\ge2\). The resulting interval certifies a strict minimax-regret design gap. For two observations per arm, all floor-optimal tables and their support transition at \(\epsilon=2-\sqrt2\) are characterized exactly. Global sufficiency of \(K_n\) is posed as a separate open frontier question and is not a theorem claim.
gap: \cite{Stoye2012LimitedValidity} solves independent-assignment contamination decisions and already reports qualitative fixed-design failures. Exact all-size fixed-count obstructions and the complete small-table support correspondence are not supplied by that result.
fill: The project evaluates the conditional obstruction, compares it exactly with the independent threshold, and solves the nine-cell floor correspondence. A Bernstein and endpoint-saddle handle isolates the unresolved global frontier.
